steps: Add the business user to your Experience Platform product profile in Adobe Admin Console to grant them system access.
Assign the user a role in the Experience Platform Permissions UI to control which features and data they can access.
Add the marketer as a user in the Admin Console to grant them access to the Experience Platform organization.
Assign the marketer a role in the Permissions UI that includes access to the required sandboxes and audience-builder features.
Create a read-only reporting role in the Permissions UI with view-only access to datasets, segments, and dashboards.
Add the new data analyst user in Admin Console and assign them the read-only reporting role so they can access reports without edit rights.
Add the user to your Adobe organization in the Admin Console so they can access Experience Platform.
Assign the Journey Optimizer journey-authoring role to the user in the Permissions UI to grant the correct access.
Add the developer to your Experience Platform product profile in the Adobe Admin Console to grant them access.
Assign the developer the required role and API credentials in the Permissions UI so they can authenticate and call Experience Platform APIs.
Add the developer to your organization in the Admin Console and generate their API credentials for the desired project.
Assign the developer's API credential to a role in the Permissions UI to grant the required sandbox and source access.
Add the data engineer as a developer in Adobe Admin Console so they can create API credentials for Experience Platform.
Assign the developer a role in the Permissions UI that grants access to the Sources and Destinations APIs so they can make authorized programmatic calls.
In the Adobe Admin Console, locate the experienced Platform user and add them to the Experience Platform product administrator role.
Confirm the user now appears under product admins so they can manage permissions, sandboxes, and configurations within Experience Platform.
Add the platform team lead as a product administrator in the Adobe Admin Console to grant them access to the product.
Assign the team lead an administrator role in the Experience Platform Permissions UI so they can manage permissions for their team.
Apply attribute-based access control labels to protected health information schema fields to mark them as sensitive and restricted.
Configure a role for external agency users that explicitly denies access to those labeled PHI fields, preventing them from viewing or activating that data.
Apply PHI data labels to sensitive health-related fields in your schema to mark them as restricted.
Configure a role in the Permissions UI to block access to those labeled fields, preventing unauthorized users from viewing health data.
Apply attribute-based access control labels to regulated financial PII schema fields to mark them as sensitive and restricted.
Create an access policy that denies any role without explicit permissions from viewing or activating those labeled financial PII fields.
Apply a GDPR-restricted data usage label to the consent schema field to mark it as sensitive and limit visibility.
Create a role-based access control policy that denies access to any field carrying that label, enforcing it across all assigned users.
Create a development sandbox and build and test your configurations, schemas, and audiences within it.
Package the validated configurations and publish them to the production sandbox for live use.
Create a development sandbox and build your new schema and ingestion pipeline inside it to test without affecting production data.
Validate that data ingests correctly into the sandbox environment, then replicate the confirmed schema and pipeline configuration in the production sandbox.
Create a new sandbox in the Admin Console and give it a name that identifies the regional business unit it will serve.
Assign the appropriate users and roles to that sandbox so the regional team has access to their dedicated environment.
Create a new sandbox in the Admin UI and designate it as an inspiration sandbox for Use Case Playbooks exploration.
Switch into the inspiration sandbox to browse and instantiate Use Case Playbooks without affecting production data.
Navigate to the Sandboxes section in the Admin UI and select the development sandbox you want to clear between project phases.
Trigger a sandbox reset to delete all assets, schemas, and data within it, leaving a clean environment ready for the next project phase.
Package the tested campaign configuration in the development sandbox by selecting its assets and publishing the sandbox package.
Import the published package into the production sandbox to deploy the campaign configuration exactly as tested.
In the source sandbox, create and publish a package containing the journey and all its dependent audience and schema assets.
Import the published package into the target sandbox to automatically recreate the journey and its dependencies without manual configuration.
Package the validated schemas and datasets in the staging sandbox and publish the package so it is ready for export.
Import the published package into the production sandbox to deploy the validated schemas and datasets.
Bundle all audience activation assets, including schemas, datasets, segments, and destinations, into a sandbox package in your development sandbox.
Publish the package and import it into your production sandbox to deploy the complete audience activation flow.
Create and publish a sandbox package containing the governance-approved data schema from the source sandbox.
Import the published package into the target regional sandbox to deploy the schema there.

workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Package the customer success journey configuration, including schemas, datasets, and journey assets, into a sandbox package and publish it.
Share the published package with the partner Adobe org and import it into their target sandbox to replicate the journey configuration.

workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Publish a sandbox package containing the compliance-approved audience model, schemas, and datasets from the source IMS org.
Import the published package into each target IMS org's sandbox to deploy the identical compliance-approved audience model across organizations.

workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Publish the co-branded campaign configuration as a sandbox package in the source organization to make it available for sharing.
Import the published package into the target organization's sandbox to replicate the campaign configuration across orgs.
Create an XDM Individual Profile schema for customer loyalty data and add identity fields such as email and loyalty ID to enable profile stitching.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested loyalty records are merged into unified customer profiles using those identity fields.
Create a new XDM Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and add field groups that capture web clickstream behavior such as page views and link clicks.
Save and enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that ingested web clickstream events can be unified into customer profiles.
Create an XDM Experience Event schema for mobile app interactions and add the Mobile SDK ExperienceEvent mixin to capture device identity fields such as IDFA and GAID.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that incoming mobile interaction events are stitched to unified profiles using those device identities.
Create an Individual Profile schema for your B2C brand and add email and CRM ID fields as primary and secondary identity descriptors.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified profiles using those identity fields.
Create an XDM Experience Event schema and add field groups for commerce transaction details and loyalty program identifiers to capture in-store purchase data.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile by designating the loyalty ID as the primary identity so purchase events can be stitched to unified customer profiles.
Create a custom field group with subscription status fields and add it to the existing profile schema in the Schema Editor.
Save the updated schema so the new subscription status fields are available for data ingestion and profile enrichment.
Create a custom field group containing your company-specific loyalty tier attributes and add it to the standard Individual Profile schema.
Save the updated schema so all datasets using it can capture and store the new loyalty tier fields in customer profiles.
Create a custom field group containing consent and preference fields, such as marketing opt-in status and data processing agreements, to capture GDPR-required information.
Add the custom consent field group to your customer profile schema so that all ingested records carry the required GDPR consent and preference attributes.
Create a custom field group containing AI propensity score attributes such as churn likelihood and purchase probability.
Add the new field group to an existing XDM Individual Profile schema so those score attributes become available on customer profiles.
Create a custom XDM class in the Schema Editor to define the new product entity type with its unique identifier and core behavior.
Build a schema based on that custom class to capture the specific product attributes needed for your catalog.
Define a reusable structured address data type containing fields like street, city, state, and postal code in the Schema Editor.
Add the saved address data type as a field to both the profile schema and the order schema so they share a consistent address structure.
Define a reference field on the product catalog schema that points to the primary identity of the customer profile schema.
Configure a schema relationship using that reference field to formally link the product catalog schema to the customer profile schema.
Define a relationship field on the order event schema that references the primary identity field of the profile schema.
Configure the schema relationship in the Schema Editor to enable joining order event records to their corresponding profile records at query time.
Create a schema using the XDM Business Account class to model your B2B account data, capturing firmographic attributes and account identifiers.
Create a second schema using the XDM Business Opportunity class and link it to the account schema to enable account-based marketing across related records.
Create an Account schema and a Contact schema in Experience Platform using the XDM Business Account and XDM Business Contact classes.
Define a relationship field on the Contact schema that references the Account schema's primary identity to establish the B2B account-contact link.
Export the finalized production schema, including all its field groups, by packaging it from the source sandbox.
Import the packaged schema into the target regional sandbox to recreate the complete schema structure there.
Open the existing customer profile schema in the Schema Editor and add a new opt-in consent field using the appropriate consent data type.
Save the updated schema so that all datasets built on it can capture and enforce the new consent field going forward.
Open an existing schema in the Schema Editor and create a custom field group containing purchase preference attributes such as preferred category, price range, and brand affinity.
Add the new custom field group to the schema and save it so that all datasets using that schema can capture and store purchase preference data.
Upload a CSV file of customer records to an Experience Platform dataset that is mapped to an XDM schema.
Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so the ingested records are merged into unified customer profiles.
Upload your daily CRM export file to a Profile-enabled dataset by creating a batch and posting the file via the Batch Ingestion API.
Close and trigger the batch so Experience Platform processes the file and merges the CRM records into unified real-time customer profiles.
Connect the FTP source connector to your landing zone and ingest the weekly loyalty tier update files as a batch dataset in Experience Platform.
Map the ingested batch data to your loyalty XDM schema so the tier updates are validated and loaded into the target dataset.
Upload a Parquet file containing customer attribute updates to Experience Platform by creating a batch against an existing dataset.
Complete and close the batch so Platform validates and ingests the Parquet records into the target dataset.
Authenticate and connect your mobile app to the Platform HTTP API streaming endpoint to begin sending real-time checkout events.
Stream the checkout event payloads to the endpoint so they are ingested immediately into Platform datasets and Real-Time Customer Profile.
Configure a streaming HTTP API source connector to receive real-time point-of-sale transaction events from retail store systems.
Validate that the streamed POS events are landing in the target dataset and appearing in customer profiles in real time.
Instrument your website with the Web SDK to capture real-time search behavior events and send them to the Edge Network.
Configure a datastream on the Edge Network to route the incoming search events into Experience Platform for immediate profile and dataset updates.
Install and configure the AEP Web SDK on your website to capture page view and cart events as XDM-formatted data.
Send the captured events through the Edge Network, which routes the data into Experience Platform for real-time profile ingestion.
Connect an Adobe Analytics report suite as a source in Experience Platform to begin streaming its data into the platform.
Map the report suite's dimensions and metrics to the corresponding XDM fields so the data conforms to the standard schema.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from Audience Manager
steps: Connect Adobe Audience Manager as a source in Experience Platform to stream your segments and traits into the platform.
Map the incoming Audience Manager segments and traits to an Experience Platform dataset so they are available for profile and segmentation use.
Configure the Marketo source connector by authenticating with your Marketo instance and selecting the lead and activity datasets to sync.
Run the dataflow so that Marketo lead and activity records stream continuously into your Platform datasets.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from cloud storage
steps: Connect your Amazon S3 bucket as a source and configure a dataflow that maps the daily transaction file fields to your target Platform dataset schema.
Set a recurring ingestion schedule on the dataflow so Platform automatically pulls each new transaction file from S3 into the dataset on a daily basis.
Configure a Salesforce CRM source connector in Experience Platform by authenticating and selecting the contact object to ingest.
Map the Salesforce contact fields to their corresponding XDM schema fields so the ingested data conforms to the unified data model.
Connect your PostgreSQL database as a source in Experience Platform by providing credentials and selecting the tables to ingest.
Configure a scheduled dataflow to run nightly incremental ingestion, pulling only new or updated records into a Platform dataset.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Stream via HTTP API
steps: Create a streaming HTTP API inlet in Experience Platform to generate a unique endpoint URL for receiving real-time data.
POST JSON event payloads to that endpoint so Experience Platform immediately updates matching real-time customer profiles with the new data.
Configure a third-party streaming source connector in Experience Platform by providing authentication credentials and mapping incoming event fields to your target XDM schema.
Activate the dataflow so that events streamed from the third-party source are continuously ingested into your Platform dataset in real time.
Open the monitoring dashboard to inspect the ingestion pipeline and identify a batch job that has failed with errors.
Diagnose the reported error details from the failed batch, correct the underlying data issue, and re-ingest the batch to complete the pipeline successfully.
Open a profile schema in the Schema Editor and mark the email, phone, and CRM ID fields as identity fields by assigning each an identity namespace.
Designate one identity field as the primary identity so Experience Platform can stitch data fragments into a unified real-time customer profile.
Open the loyalty program ID field in the schema editor and mark it as the primary identity, assigning it to the appropriate identity namespace.
Open the email field in the same schema and mark it as a secondary identity so Experience Platform links both fields when building unified profiles.
Open the Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and select the ECID field to configure its identity descriptor.
Enable the identity toggle, choose the Identity namespace as ECID, and mark it as the primary identity for that schema.
Ingest customer records containing multiple identity fields, such as email, phone, and CRM ID, into Experience Platform.
Identity Service automatically links those identity fields to build a unified identity graph connecting all records to a single profile.
Ingest web, mobile, and CRM data into Experience Platform, each carrying identity namespaces such as ECID, email, and customer ID.
Identity Service links those namespaces into a unified identity graph, stitching all cross-channel interactions into a single customer view.
Capture the anonymous visitor's ECID from their website session and record their browsing behavior against that temporary identity.
When the visitor logs in, Identity Service links their ECID to their known Customer ID, merging the anonymous activity into their unified real-time profile.
Capture the mobile device ID collected during anonymous app browsing and link it to the customer's authenticated identity namespace at the moment of login.
Identity Service merges the device ID into the existing customer profile, unifying all prior anonymous interactions with the known customer's profile in real time.
Capture the email address submitted during guest checkout on the order confirmation page and send it to Identity Service as a new identity event.
Identity Service matches the submitted email to an existing known profile, merging the anonymous visitor's activity into the unified customer profile via the identity graph.
Search for a VIP customer in the Identity Service using a known identifier such as their email or loyalty ID.
Inspect the customer's identity graph to confirm all cross-channel identities, including web, mobile, and CRM, are correctly linked.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Ingest your CRM records into a dataset built on a schema that has an identity field and a Profile-enabled class.
Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so each ingested CRM record is stitched into a unified customer profile via the identity graph.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Ingest loyalty transaction data into a dataset built on a profile-enabled schema in Experience Platform.
Toggle the dataset's Real-Time Customer Profile switch on so loyalty transactions are merged into unified customer profiles.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Instrument your mobile app with the Mobile SDK to stream behavioral event data into Experience Platform datasets backed by a Profile-enabled schema.
Once ingested, Experience Platform merges the mobile event data into unified real-time customer profiles via the identity graph, making them available for personalization.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Create a merge policy in the Platform UI and set the attribute merge to Dataset Precedence, placing your CRM dataset above third-party datasets in the priority order.
Save and activate the merge policy so that unified profiles are built using CRM attribute values whenever conflicts arise with third-party data.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Create a merge policy for the B2B account profile view and set the merge method to dataset precedence, ordering your trusted account datasets from highest to lowest priority.
Save and activate the merge policy so that when profile fragments are stitched, attributes from higher-priority account datasets override those from lower-priority sources.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Create a merge policy in the Real-Time Customer Profile settings, selecting timestamp-ordered last-write-wins as the attribute merge strategy.
Assign the merge policy to your streaming-enabled dataset so that the most recently ingested attribute values always overwrite older ones in the unified profile.
Define a computed attribute using a sum aggregation on the purchase amount field, scoped to a 30-day lookback window.
Enable the computed attribute so it automatically calculates and updates each customer's total purchase amount on their real-time profile.
Define a computed attribute in the Profile UI that counts the number of app session events occurring within the past 7 days.
Enable and publish the computed attribute so it is continuously calculated and available on each customer's real-time profile for segmentation and personalization.
Define a computed attribute rule that calculates a recency score by referencing the customer's most recent purchase event date from their real-time profile.
Publish the computed attribute so it is continuously evaluated and appended to each customer's unified profile for use in segmentation and personalization.
Identify the former customer's identity namespace and ID, then submit a profile delete job targeting their unified profile in the profile store.
Confirm the delete job completes successfully, verifying the former customer's data has been fully removed from the Real-Time Customer Profile store.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
steps: Send a Profile Upsert API request with the customer's identity and updated email opt-out preference field to write the new attribute value into their profile.
Verify the updated email opt-out preference is reflected in the customer's unified real-time profile by retrieving it via the Profile Access API.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
steps: Make a streaming upsert API call to the Profile Store with the customer's updated consent revocation attributes, targeting their identity.
Experience Platform immediately overwrites the stored consent fields on the unified profile, halting any downstream activations that depend on consent.
Navigate to the Union Schema view in Real-Time Customer Profile to see all merged attributes contributed by every schema sharing the same class.
Use the consolidated list of available attributes from the union schema to inform and build precise segment definitions in the Segment Builder.
In Segment Builder, define an audience of customers who have a product view event but no corresponding purchase event within the same time window.
Save the audience to make it available for activation in re-engagement campaigns targeting those browsing customers.
Open Segment Builder and define a rule filtering profiles where the lifetime spend attribute exceeds your chosen threshold value.
Save and publish the segment to create a high-value customer audience ready for activation.
In Segment Builder, add a rule filtering profiles where the email open event occurred within the last 7 days.
Save and publish the segment to create an audience of customers who recently opened an email.
In Segment Builder, add a rule filtering profiles where the days-since-last-purchase attribute exceeds your churn-risk threshold, such as 90 days.
Save and publish the segment to create a churn-risk audience ready for activation to re-engagement campaigns.
In Segment Builder, define an audience rule that matches loyalty program members whose last site visit attribute is more than 60 days ago.
Save and publish the audience so it is available for activation in re-engagement campaigns targeting those lapsed loyalty members.
Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
Build an audience in Segment Builder by filtering profiles whose Customer AI propensity score exceeds your defined threshold.
Ingest both in-store and online purchase history data into Experience Platform and merge them into unified real-time customer profiles.
Use Segment Builder to define a holiday campaign audience by combining rules that filter profiles based on in-store and online purchase activity.
In Segment Builder, switch to account profiles and add a filter for open opportunities where deal size exceeds your defined revenue threshold.
Save the segment to generate a B2B audience of high-value accounts ready for activation to sales or advertising destinations.
Enable streaming segmentation on an audience rule that fires when a customer views a product page, qualifying them instantly as they browse.
Use the continuously updated audience membership to trigger real-time personalization or journey actions for those customers.
Configure a streaming segment that qualifies customers in real time the moment they add an item to their cart.
Trigger a push notification journey automatically when a customer qualifies for that audience.
Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers who completed a browsing session without making a purchase, so they are evaluated in real time as session-end events arrive.
Activate the streaming audience to your re-engagement destination so matched customers receive a personalized follow-up message within seconds of their session ending.
Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers the moment their cumulative spend crosses the VIP threshold, evaluated in real time as each purchase event arrives.
Activate the VIP segment to your personalization and messaging destinations so customers receive VIP treatment instantly upon qualification.
Create a new audience targeting customers likely to buy weather-related products and trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job to evaluate it immediately.
Once the batch job completes and profiles are populated, activate the fully evaluated audience to your campaign destination without waiting for the next scheduled run.
Manually trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job for the target audience to force evaluation outside the scheduled window.
Once the evaluation job completes and the audience membership is refreshed, activate the updated audience to your destination for the flash-sale campaign.
Send a Segment Match connection request to your retail partner by entering their IMS organization ID and configuring the data sharing terms.
Once the partner accepts the connection, select and share the approved audience segments with them through the established Segment Match feed.
Create a high-intent buyer audience in Segment Builder and configure a Segment Match feed to share it with your media partner.
Your media partner accepts the Segment Match feed and receives the overlapping audience for activation in their own Platform instance.
Accept the shared segment sent by your CPG partner through Segment Match to receive their audience into your sandbox.
Activate the received partner audience to your advertising destination to run a prospecting campaign against it.
Authenticate to Facebook Custom Audiences by providing your Facebook account credentials and granting the required permissions in the destination configuration.
Complete the destination setup by specifying the connection details, data export settings, and saving the configured Facebook Custom Audiences destination in Platform.
Configure and authenticate a new Google Ads destination in the Destinations catalog by providing your account credentials and connection settings.
Activate your first-party audience to the connected Google Ads destination to enable targeted ad delivery.
Authenticate and configure a new LinkedIn Matched Audiences destination in the Destinations catalog by providing your LinkedIn account credentials and mapping settings.
Activate your B2B account-based audience to the connected LinkedIn destination so matched accounts receive targeted ads.
Connect your email service provider as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the connection settings.
Select the high-value customer audience and activate it to that email service provider destination for campaign delivery.
Connect your CRM platform as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the authentication and mapping settings.
Activate your churn-risk audience to that connected CRM destination so sales and retention teams can launch targeted outreach.
Connect a programmatic display advertising destination in Experience Platform and configure the connection credentials and mapping settings.
Activate the cart abandonment audience to that connected destination so ads are served to those shoppers across the display network.
Connect your Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account as a destination in Experience Platform.
Select the raw events dataset and activate it to that Azure Data Lake destination for downstream analysis.
Connect a cloud storage destination and select the dataset containing profile attribute data to export.
Configure a nightly export schedule so the dataset is automatically delivered to the cloud storage bucket each night.
Configure the Azure Blob Storage destination by providing your storage account credentials, container name, and scheduled export settings.
Activate the desired audience to the configured Azure Blob destination so membership data is exported on the defined schedule.
Build a high-intent B2B audience in Real-Time CDP by segmenting profiles based on product interest signals and account attributes.
Connect the Marketo Engage destination and activate that audience so matched leads are automatically enrolled in Marketo nurturing sequences.
Connect the Google Customer Match destination and map your first-party email identity fields to the required Google attributes.
Activate your email audience to the configured Google Customer Match destination so Google can match profiles for search retargeting.
Build a seed audience of your highest-value customers in Real-Time CDP to use as the lookalike source for Facebook Ads prospecting.
Connect the Facebook Custom Audiences destination and activate the seed audience so Facebook can generate a lookalike audience to reach new prospective customers.
Connect the LiveRamp destination and activate your first-party audience by mapping identity fields such as email or phone to LiveRamp's RampID.
LiveRamp distributes the resolved RampIDs to connected TV and addressable media partners, enabling privacy-safe audience targeting across those channels.
Connect a Snowflake batch data share destination and activate the target Platform audience to it.
The data science team queries the shared Snowflake dataset to access the audience profiles for their analysis.
Build a high-value customer audience in Real-Time CDP and connect Adobe Target as an activation destination.
Activate the audience to Adobe Target so it can personalize homepage content in real time for those customers.
Connect Adobe Target as a destination and activate a Real-Time CDP audience with profile attributes, such as product preferences and purchase history, to Target.
Use those streamed profile attributes inside Target to deliver personalized product recommendations to each visitor in real time.
Configure and train a Customer AI churn propensity model by selecting the dataset, defining the churn event, and running the model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
Build an audience segment filtered to customers with high churn propensity scores and activate it to a campaign destination to deliver a personalized win-back offer.
Configure a Customer AI model with purchase propensity as the goal, select the input dataset, and run the model to generate propensity scores for each profile.
Build an audience by filtering profiles above the high-intent score threshold and activate that audience to your advertising or email destination.
Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate upsell propensity scores for each customer profile.
Build an audience segment using the propensity score threshold and activate it to your campaign destination.
Configure and run a Customer AI churn prediction model to generate propensity-to-churn scores for each customer profile.
Build an audience of high-churn-risk customers using those propensity scores and activate them into a don't-lose retention journey.
Configure a Customer AI model using behavioral data to predict which users are at risk of uninstalling the app.
Run the model to generate propensity scores and build an audience of high-risk users from those scores.
Activate the at-risk audience to your mobile and advertising destinations to deliver targeted re-engagement campaigns.
Configure an Attribution AI instance by defining conversion events and mapping marketing touchpoints across channels.
Run the Attribution AI model to generate attribution scores for each touchpoint in the customer journey.
Analyze the attribution results to measure each channel's contribution to conversions and calculate ROI.
Configure and run an Attribution AI model instance, selecting the conversion events and marketing touchpoints to analyze.
Review the generated attribution scores and channel performance insights to see which channels drive the most conversions.
Reallocate your marketing budget toward the highest-performing channels identified by the Attribution AI results.
Configure an Attribution AI instance by selecting your conversion events, touchpoint channels, and attribution model to generate multi-touch credit scores.
Run the Attribution AI model to produce channel-level attribution scores and surface the results as a dataset in Experience Platform.
Connect the Attribution AI scores dataset to Customer Journey Analytics and build an executive dashboard visualizing channel contribution and conversion impact.
Connect to Query Service and write a SQL query targeting the Platform dataset that contains your web analytics and marketing channel data.
Execute the query to aggregate and calculate unique visitor counts grouped by each marketing channel.
Review the returned results to compare visitor volumes across channels and export the data for reporting.
Ingest a batch of customer data into an Experience Platform dataset.
Run a SQL query in Query Service against the ingested dataset to check field values, null counts, and record totals.
Review the query results to confirm data quality and flag any records that fail validation rules.
Connect to Query Service and write a SQL query that aggregates behavioral event data to calculate each customer's total spend and purchase frequency.
Run a CTAS query to materialize the aggregated results as a new derived dataset stored in Experience Platform.
Enable the derived dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so high-value customer attributes are available for segmentation and activation.
Connect Tableau to Query Service using the PostgreSQL credentials provided in the Experience Platform UI.
Write a SQL query in Tableau to pull audience membership and performance metrics from the platform datasets.
Build an interactive visualization in Tableau dashboarding the audience performance results from the query.
Open Query Service and write a SQL query that filters customer profiles with no purchase events in the last 30 days.
Run the query against your Experience Platform datasets to retrieve the list of inactive customers.
Save the query results as a new dataset to build an audience for re-engagement campaigns.
Write a SQL query in Query Service that analyzes event history to calculate churn-indicator features such as days since last activity and session frequency.
Execute the SQL query to materialize the results as a new derived dataset stored in Experience Platform.
Use the derived churn-indicator dataset to build segments or feed AI models for churn prediction.
Ingest streaming events into Experience Platform so they land in a dataset backed by your target XDM schema.
Run a Query Service SQL query against the dataset to inspect field values, types, and structure of the ingested events.
Compare the query results against the expected XDM schema fields to confirm all events conform and flag any mismatches.
Open the schema containing contractually restricted third-party data fields in the Schema Editor.
Select each restricted field and apply the appropriate DULE data usage labels to mark them as third-party contractual data.
Save the labeled schema so downstream governance policies can enforce restrictions on those fields.
Open an existing profile schema in the Schema Editor and identify the fields that contain personally identifiable information.
Apply the appropriate sensitive personal data usage labels to each PII field to mark them as restricted.
Save the labeled schema so that downstream data governance policies can enforce restrictions on those fields.
Open the event schema in the Schema Editor and navigate to the device ID fields that should not be used for identity stitching.
Apply the appropriate data usage labels, such as I2 or device-linkage restriction labels, directly to those device ID fields.
Create a data governance policy that enforces those labels to block identity stitching operations on the labeled device ID fields.
Apply restrictive data usage labels to the schema fields that contain sensitive customer data.
Navigate to Data Governance policies and create a new policy that references those applied labels.
Define the policy rule to block activation of those labeled fields to advertising network destinations.
Apply sensitive health data usage labels to the schema fields that contain patient or medical information.
Create a data usage policy that restricts any data labeled as health information from being activated to social media destinations.
Enforce the policy so that any activation attempt to a social media destination containing health-labeled data is automatically blocked.
Apply a restrictive data usage label to a schema field containing sensitive customer data.
Create a data usage policy that prohibits activating data with that label to advertising destinations.
Attempt to activate an audience containing that labeled data and verify the platform automatically blocks it.
Apply data usage labels to sensitive schema fields to classify the data as restricted for advertising use.
Create a data usage policy that blocks activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
Attempt to activate the audience to an ad destination and confirm the policy violation is enforced and blocked.
Apply HIPAA-aligned data usage labels to sensitive health-related schema fields to mark them as restricted for marketing use.
Create data usage policies that block those labeled fields from being activated to advertising or third-party marketing destinations.
Activate a compliant patient audience to an approved destination, letting Platform enforce the policies and block any violations automatically.
Submit a GDPR data access job via the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity and regulation type.
Privacy Service locates and compiles all stored data associated with that customer identity across Experience Platform datasets.
Download the exported data package from the completed job and deliver it to the customer to fulfill the access request.
Submit a CCPA deletion request to Privacy Service by providing the customer's identity details and namespace.
Privacy Service propagates the deletion job to all connected Platform services that hold the customer's data.
Confirm the deletion is complete by reviewing the job status once all services report successful erasure.
Install the AEP Privacy JavaScript library on your website to capture visitor opt-out signals.
Configure the library to detect and collect opt-out preferences submitted by site visitors.
Forward the collected opt-out signals to Adobe Privacy Service for processing and compliance enforcement.
Authenticate with the Privacy Service REST API and construct a JSON payload containing the data subject identities and the type of privacy request to submit.
POST the payload to the Privacy Service API endpoint to programmatically create delete or access jobs at scale for all relevant Experience Cloud products.
Poll the API for job status updates and retrieve the completed results to confirm each privacy request has been fulfilled.
Register a webhook or event listener by subscribing to Privacy Service events in the Adobe Developer Console.
Submit a privacy deletion request through the Privacy Service API to trigger a job.
Receive a real-time event notification when the deletion job completes and log the result for compliance tracking.
Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert types.
Select the segment job failure alert and subscribe to it with your email or notification preference.
Receive an immediate notification when an audience evaluation job fails so you can investigate and resolve the issue.
