workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Package the customer success journey configuration, including schemas, datasets, and journey assets, into a sandbox package.
Publish the package and share it with the partner Adobe org using cross-org package sharing.
The partner org imports the package into their sandbox to deploy the customer success journey configuration.

workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Package the compliance-approved audience model and its dependent assets into a sandbox tooling package.
Publish the package and share it with the target IMS organizations via the cross-org sharing feature.
Each recipient org imports the package into their sandbox, making the audience model available for activation.

workflows.source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
steps: Package the co-branded campaign configuration, including schemas and audiences, into a sandbox package.
Publish the package and generate a shareable link to distribute it to the partner organization.
Import the shared package into the partner org's sandbox to replicate the campaign configuration.
Create an XDM Individual Profile schema in the Schema Editor to represent your customer loyalty data structure.
Add identity fields such as email or loyalty ID to the schema and mark them as primary and secondary identities.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so loyalty data can be merged into unified customer profiles.
Create a new XDM Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor to capture web clickstream behavior.
Add the required field groups, such as Web Details and Environment Details, to include clickstream-specific fields.
Save and enable the schema so datasets can be created from it to ingest web interaction data.
Create an XDM Experience Event schema and add the Mobile App Details and Environment field groups to capture mobile app interaction events.
Add the Identity Map field group to the schema to store device identifiers such as IDFA and GAID for identity resolution.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so mobile app events are stitched into unified profiles using those device identities.
Create an XDM Individual Profile schema for your B2C brand and add the required field groups for personal details and CRM attributes.
Define email address and CRM ID fields as identity descriptors, setting one as the primary identity for profile stitching.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified customer profiles.
Create an XDM ExperienceEvent schema and add the Commerce Details field group to capture transaction data like purchase amount and items.
Add the IdentityMap field group and define loyalty card ID and email as identity fields to link the event to a customer profile.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested in-store purchase events contribute to unified customer profiles.
Create a custom field group defining subscription status fields such as plan type, renewal date, and opt-in flag.
Add the new custom field group to your existing profile schema in the Schema Editor.
Save the updated schema so subscription status fields are available for data ingestion and profile attributes.
Create a custom field group defining company-specific loyalty tier attributes such as tier name, points balance, and enrollment date.
Add the custom field group to your standard Individual Profile schema to extend it with those loyalty tier fields.
Save the updated schema so that datasets and profiles can capture and store loyalty tier data for your customers.
Create a custom field group in the Schema Editor and add consent and preference fields required for GDPR compliance.
Add the custom consent field group to your XDM Individual Profile schema and save the schema.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that consent preferences are captured and enforced on every unified customer profile.
Create a custom field group containing AI propensity score attributes such as churn likelihood and purchase probability.
Add the custom field group to an existing XDM Individual Profile schema in the Schema Editor.
Save the updated schema so propensity score attributes are available for ingestion and segmentation in Real-Time Customer Profile.
Create a custom XDM class to represent the new product entity type, defining its core identity and behavior.
Create a schema that uses the new custom class as its base structure for the product catalog.
Add field groups to the schema to capture all required product attributes and relationships.
Create a reusable structured address data type with fields like street, city, state, and postal code.
Add the address data type to a customer profile schema to capture residential address information.
Add the same address data type to an order schema to capture shipping and billing addresses.
Define a reference field on the product catalog schema that will serve as the join key to the customer profile schema.
Open the relationship editor and configure the reference field to point to the primary identity of the customer profile schema.
Save the relationship so the product catalog schema is linked and can be used in segmentation and queries alongside customer profiles.
Define a source schema for order events and a destination schema for profiles, ensuring both have a primary identity field configured.
In the source order event schema, add a relationship descriptor that references the primary identity field of the destination profile schema.
Save the relationship so that Query Service and Customer Journey Analytics can join order event records to their corresponding profile records.
Create a B2B Account schema using the XDM Business Account class to capture company-level attributes for ABM targeting.
Create a B2B Opportunity schema using the XDM Business Opportunity class and link it to the Account schema via a relationship field.
Enable both schemas for Real-Time Customer Profile so account and opportunity data can be unified and used in ABM campaigns.
Finalize the production schema by ensuring all required field groups are added and the schema is fully configured.
Package the schema using the sandbox tooling, bundling all associated field groups into an exportable package.
Import the package into the target regional sandbox to recreate the schema with all its field groups intact.
Open the existing customer profile schema in the Schema Editor and add a new field for opt-in consent using the appropriate data type.
Assign the new consent field to the correct field group and save the updated schema definition.
Verify the updated schema is reflected in the associated dataset so incoming consent data maps to the new field correctly.
Create a custom field group containing purchase preference attributes such as preferred category, price range, and brand affinity.
Add the custom field group to the existing schema by editing the schema in the Schema Editor.
Save the updated schema so downstream datasets and profiles can capture the new purchase preference attributes.
Upload a CSV file of customer records to Experience Platform using the batch ingestion workflow.
Map the CSV fields to an XDM schema and complete the batch ingestion job to create a dataset.
Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified profiles.
Upload the daily CRM export file to a Platform dataset by creating a batch and posting the file via the batch ingestion API.
Close and finalize the batch so Platform validates and ingests the records into the dataset.
Confirm the ingested records are merged into Real-Time Customer Profile by verifying profile counts in the monitoring dashboard.
Connect the FTP landing zone as a source connector in Experience Platform to access the weekly loyalty tier update files.
Map the FTP file fields to your loyalty schema and ingest the batch data into the corresponding Platform dataset.
Verify the batch ingestion run succeeded and confirm updated loyalty tier records appear in customer profiles.
Upload a Parquet file containing customer attribute updates to Experience Platform using the batch ingestion API.
Monitor the batch ingestion job to confirm the file is successfully processed and validated.
Verify the ingested records appear in the target Platform dataset with updated customer attributes.
Register a streaming inlet using the HTTP API Source to create an authenticated endpoint for your mobile app.
Send real-time checkout event payloads from the mobile app to that streaming endpoint using HTTP POST requests.
Verify the streamed events land in the Platform dataset and are merged into real-time customer profiles.
Connect your retail point-of-sale systems to Platform using the Streaming Ingestion API or an HTTP Source connector.
Stream transaction events in real time so Platform ingests each sale as it occurs at the register.
Verify the incoming data in the dataset activity view to confirm records are landing correctly in Platform.
Instrument your website with the Web SDK to capture real-time search behavior events as they occur.
The Web SDK sends those events to the Edge Network, which forwards them to Experience Platform as a streaming data flow.
The streamed events land in a dataset and update Real-Time Customer Profiles with the latest search behavior.
Install and configure the AEP Web SDK on your website to capture page view and cart events from visitors.
The Web SDK sends those events in real time through the Edge Network, which validates and routes the data to Experience Platform.
The ingested events land in your configured dataset and are merged into real-time customer profiles for immediate use.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from Audience Manager
steps: Connect Adobe Audience Manager as a source to begin streaming segments and traits into Experience Platform.
Map the incoming Audience Manager traits and segments to an XDM schema for standardized data representation.
Verify the mapped data lands in an Experience Platform dataset ready for profile and segmentation use.
Configure the Marketo source connector by authenticating with your Munchkin ID and mapping lead and activity objects to XDM schemas.
Run the dataflow to ingest Marketo lead and activity records into Platform datasets in batch or streaming mode.
Verify that the ingested records are merged into unified Real-Time Customer Profiles via the identity graph.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from cloud storage
steps: Connect your Amazon S3 bucket as a source in Experience Platform and select the daily transaction files to ingest.
Map the source file fields to your target XDM schema and configure a recurring daily dataflow schedule.
Run the scheduled dataflow to load each day's transaction files into the target Platform dataset automatically.
Configure a Salesforce CRM source connector by authenticating with your Salesforce credentials and selecting the contact object to ingest.
Map the Salesforce contact fields to their corresponding XDM schema fields using the field mapping interface.
Run the dataflow to ingest the mapped Salesforce contact records into your Platform dataset.
Connect your PostgreSQL database to Experience Platform by configuring a source connector with your credentials.
Map the database table fields to your target XDM schema to define how the data will land in Platform.
Schedule a nightly incremental dataflow so only new or updated records are ingested into Platform automatically.

workflows.source: Data Ingestion / Stream via HTTP API
steps: Create a streaming HTTP API inlet in Experience Platform to generate a unique endpoint URL for receiving data.
POST JSON event payloads to that endpoint URL from your application or server in real time.
Experience Platform processes the incoming events and immediately updates the matching real-time customer profiles.
Ingest a batch of customer data into Experience Platform and open the monitoring dashboard to track its progress.
Identify the failed batch job in the dashboard by reviewing the error details and failure reason provided.
Correct the data issues in the source file and re-ingest the batch to complete successful ingestion.
Open your profile schema in the Schema Editor and select the email, phone, and CRM ID fields you want to designate as identities.
Mark each selected field as an identity field and assign the appropriate identity namespace, such as Email, Phone, or a custom CRM ID namespace.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so the labeled identity fields are used to stitch records into unified profiles via the identity graph.
Open your loyalty schema in the Schema Editor and mark the loyalty program ID field as the primary identity namespace.
Locate the email field in the same schema and label it as a secondary identity namespace.
Save the schema so Experience Platform uses the loyalty ID to anchor unified profiles and email as a supporting identity link.
Create an Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and add the ECID field from the Experience Cloud ID namespace.
Mark the ECID field as the primary identity on the schema to designate it as the main identifier for events.
Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so incoming events are stitched into unified profiles using the ECID.
Ingest customer records containing multiple identity fields such as email, phone, and CRM ID into Experience Platform.
Identity Service processes the ingested data and links the identity fields into a unified identity graph for each customer.
Use the identity graph to merge profile fragments into a single real-time customer profile across all touchpoints.
Ingest customer data from your website, mobile app, and CRM, each carrying their own identifiers such as cookies, device IDs, and email addresses.
Identity Service links those identifiers across sources into a single identity graph, resolving all fragments to one unified customer profile.
Query the identity graph to trace a customer's full cross-channel journey using any known identifier as the starting point.
Capture an anonymous visitor's web interactions using the Web SDK, assigning them a temporary ECID.
When the visitor logs in, send their authenticated identity so the identity graph links the ECID to their known Customer ID.
Experience Platform merges the anonymous and authenticated profiles into a single unified real-time customer profile.
Capture the anonymous mobile device ID collected during pre-login app browsing as an identity in the identity graph.
When the customer logs into the app, link the mobile device ID to their authenticated customer ID via Identity Service.
Identity Service merges the anonymous device activity into the existing customer profile, creating a complete unified view.
Capture the anonymous visitor's browsing session under a temporary ECID during guest checkout.
At order confirmation, collect the customer's email address and send it to Identity Service alongside the ECID.
Identity Service stitches the email to the existing ECID, merging the anonymous session into the known customer profile.
Search for the VIP customer in Identity Service by entering one of their known identifiers, such as email or CRM ID.
Open the identity graph viewer to see all identities linked to that customer across channels and devices.
Confirm that all expected cross-channel identifiers, such as mobile ID, web cookie, and loyalty ID, are correctly stitched together in the graph.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Ingest your CRM records into a dataset built on a schema with the correct identity fields defined.
Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records are merged into unified profiles.
Verify that the CRM records appear as unified customer profiles in the Profile viewer.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Create a schema for loyalty transaction data and enable it for Real-Time Customer Profile.
Create a dataset using that schema and ingest loyalty transaction records into it.
Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so loyalty data enriches unified customer profiles.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Instrument your mobile app with the Mobile SDK to stream real-time event data into Experience Platform.
Map the incoming event data to an XDM schema and ingest it into a Profile-enabled dataset.
Experience Platform stitches the mobile events into unified real-time customer profiles ready for personalization.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Navigate to the Merge Policies section in the Real-Time Customer Profile settings and create a new merge policy.
Configure the merge policy to use a custom dataset precedence order, placing your CRM dataset above any third-party data datasets.
Save and set the merge policy as active so unified profiles are built using CRM data as the authoritative source.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Enable your B2B account datasets for Real-Time Customer Profile so their data is available for merging.
Create a new merge policy and set the merge method to dataset precedence, ordering your B2B account datasets by priority.
Apply the merge policy to your account profile view so that profile lookups reflect the correct dataset precedence.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
steps: Create a merge policy in the Profile settings and select timestamp-ordered last-write-wins as the attribute merge method.
Assign the relevant union schema and enable the merge policy as the default for your streaming ingestion datasets.
Verify that incoming streaming records update unified profiles correctly by checking that the most recent attribute values always take precedence.
Define a computed attribute in the Profile UI that sums the total purchase amount from experience events in the last 30 days.
Enable and publish the computed attribute so Platform continuously calculates and updates the value on each customer profile.
Use the computed attribute as a condition in Segment Builder to build audiences based on each customer's rolling 30-day spend.
Define a computed attribute that counts the number of app session events occurring in the past 7 days.
Publish the computed attribute so it continuously updates on each customer's real-time profile.
Use the computed attribute in Segment Builder to create audiences based on recent app session activity.
Identify the former customer's identity namespace and identity value to target their profile for deletion.
Submit a profile delete job via the Profile System Jobs API using the customer's identity details.
Monitor the delete job status until it completes, confirming the customer's data is removed from the profile store.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
steps: Identify the customer's profile by their identity namespace and ID to target the correct record.
Send a Profile Upsert API request with the updated email opt-out preference field value for that customer.
Verify the unified profile now reflects the new opt-out preference in Real-Time Customer Profile.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
steps: Receive a customer's consent revocation event and prepare the updated consent attributes for ingestion.
Send an API upsert call to the Real-Time Customer Profile endpoint to immediately overwrite the stored consent fields.
Verify the profile reflects the revoked consent so downstream journeys and activations respect the updated preference.
Enable your XDM schemas for Real-Time Customer Profile so their fields contribute to the union schema.
Navigate to the Union Schema view in the platform to see all merged attributes across every enabled schema for a given class.
Use those discovered attributes to define precise segment conditions in the Segment Builder.
Define a segment rule that includes customers who viewed a product page within a recent time window.
Add an exclusion rule to filter out any customers who completed a purchase for that product.
Save and activate the resulting audience to re-engage those browsing customers across your channels.
Open Segment Builder and add the lifetime spend attribute with a threshold rule to filter high-value customers.
Preview the estimated audience size to confirm the threshold captures the right customer segment.
Save and publish the audience so it is available for activation to downstream destinations.
Open Segment Builder and add an event rule filtering for email open events within the last 7 days.
Review the estimated audience size to confirm the rule captures the right customers.
Save and publish the audience for use in campaigns or journeys.
Open Segment Builder and add a days-since-last-purchase attribute rule, setting a threshold that identifies customers who have not purchased recently.
Review the estimated audience size to confirm the rule captures the intended churn-risk population, then save the segment definition.
Publish the churn-risk audience so it is available for activation in re-engagement journeys and campaigns.
Define a segment rule that filters for loyalty program members using their profile attributes.
Add a behavioral condition to exclude any member who has visited the site in the last 60 days.
Save the audience and activate it to a re-engagement channel to bring inactive members back.
Ingest both in-store and online purchase history data into Experience Platform and merge them into unified real-time customer profiles.
Open Segment Builder and define rules that combine in-store purchase attributes with online purchase events to identify holiday shoppers.
Save and publish the audience for activation in your holiday campaign channels.
Connect your CRM and ingest account and opportunity data into Experience Platform using a B2B source connector.
In Segment Builder, filter accounts linked to open opportunities where the deal size exceeds your defined revenue threshold.
Save and activate the B2B account audience to your sales engagement or advertising destination.
Stream page-view events from the website into Experience Platform using the Web SDK as customers browse.
Evaluate incoming events against a product-interest segment rule in real time using streaming segmentation.
Qualify customers into the segment instantly and activate the updated audience to a personalization destination.
Define a streaming segment that qualifies customers the moment they add an item to their cart.
The customer adds an item to their cart, triggering instant audience qualification in real time.
Fire a push notification to the qualified customer immediately, driving them back to complete their purchase.
Capture a real-time session-end event with no purchase via the Web SDK as a streaming event into Experience Platform.
A streaming segment rule evaluates the event instantly and qualifies the customer for the re-engagement audience in real time.
Trigger a re-engagement journey that delivers a personalized message to the customer immediately after their session ends.
Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers whose cumulative spend crosses your VIP threshold in real time.
As a customer's next purchase pushes their total spend over the threshold, the streaming engine instantly adds them to the VIP segment.
Activate the VIP audience to your personalization and loyalty destinations to immediately deliver VIP-tier experiences.
Create a new audience segment targeting customers likely to respond to a weather-related product promotion.
Trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job to immediately evaluate and populate the audience without waiting for the scheduled run.
Activate the freshly evaluated audience to your campaign destination to launch the urgent weather-related promotion.
Open the audience in Segment Builder and trigger a manual on-demand batch evaluation job to refresh membership ahead of schedule.
Wait for the evaluation job to complete and verify the updated audience membership counts reflect current customer data.
Activate the freshly evaluated audience to your destination to power the unexpected flash-sale campaign immediately.
Configure a Segment Match connection by sending a connection request to your retail partner using their IMS org ID.
Once the partner accepts the connection, select the audience segments you want to share and define the match keys for identity overlap.
Publish the Segment Match feed so your retail partner can receive and activate the shared audience in their sandbox.
Create a high-intent buyer audience in Segment Builder using behavioral and purchase signals.
Set up a Segment Match connection by sending a feed invitation to your media partner organization.
Share the high-intent buyer audience through the accepted Segment Match feed for the partner to activate.
Accept an incoming Segment Match share from a CPG partner to receive their audience data into your sandbox.
Combine the received partner segment with your own profile data to build a refined prospecting audience.
Activate the prospecting audience to your advertising destination to launch a targeted prospecting campaign.
Navigate to the Destinations catalog and select Facebook Custom Audiences, then authenticate by connecting your Facebook ad account.
Configure the destination by specifying the account ID, data mapping, and identity fields to match Platform profiles to Facebook users.
Save the configured destination so it is available to receive and activate audiences from Platform.
Navigate to the Destinations catalog and select Google Ads to begin configuring the connection with your account credentials.
Authenticate and configure the destination by mapping your first-party identity fields to the Google Ads customer match parameters.
Activate your first-party audience to the connected Google Ads destination to enable targeted ad delivery.
Authenticate and configure a LinkedIn Matched Audiences destination connection in the Destinations catalog.
Map your account-based audience segments to the LinkedIn destination, matching profile attributes to LinkedIn's required identity fields.
Activate the mapped B2B audiences to LinkedIn so matched accounts receive targeted advertising campaigns.
Build a high-value customer audience using profile attributes and purchase behavior in Segment Builder.
Connect your email service provider as a destination in Experience Platform.
Activate the high-value audience to that email destination to launch your campaign.
Build a churn-risk audience by segmenting profiles that show high likelihood of churning based on behavioral signals.
Connect your CRM platform as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the field mappings.
Activate the churn-risk audience to the CRM destination so your retention team can launch targeted outreach campaigns.
Build a cart abandonment audience by segmenting profiles of customers who added items but did not complete checkout.
Connect a programmatic display advertising destination and configure the mapping and activation settings.
Activate the cart abandonment audience to that destination to serve targeted display ads to those shoppers.
Connect an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 destination in Experience Platform using your account credentials.
Select the raw events dataset you want to export and map it to the connected Azure Data Lake destination.
Schedule and run the dataset export so the raw events land in Azure Data Lake for downstream analysis.
Connect a cloud storage destination by providing your bucket credentials and authentication details in the Destinations catalog.
Select the profile attribute dataset you want to export and map the relevant fields to the destination schema.
Configure a nightly export schedule so Platform automatically delivers the profile attribute data to your cloud storage bucket each night.
Connect to the Azure Blob destination by providing your storage account credentials and container details.
Configure a scheduled export by setting the file format, export frequency, and file naming conventions for the audience data.
Activate your target audience to the Azure Blob destination so membership exports are delivered to your container on schedule.
Build a high-intent B2B audience in Real-Time CDP by segmenting profiles based on product engagement and firmographic attributes.
Connect Marketo Engage as a destination and map the audience fields to the corresponding Marketo lead attributes.
Activate the audience to Marketo Engage so matched leads automatically enroll in the appropriate nurturing sequences.
Build an audience of known customers using their hashed email addresses in Real-Time CDP.
Connect to the Google Customer Match destination and map the hashed email identity field.
Activate the audience to Google Customer Match to enable search retargeting for those customers.
Build a seed audience of your highest-value existing customers using profile attributes and behaviors in Segment Builder.
Connect your Facebook Ads account as a destination and activate the seed audience to Facebook Custom Audiences.
Facebook uses the seed audience to generate a lookalike audience, expanding your reach to new prospective customers.
Connect the LiveRamp destination in Experience Platform and authenticate with your LiveRamp account credentials.
Select your first-party audience and activate it to the LiveRamp destination for identity resolution and distribution.
LiveRamp distributes the resolved audience to connected TV and addressable media partners for targeted campaign delivery.
Configure and train a Customer AI model to predict churn propensity scores for each customer profile.
Once scoring is complete, build a segment targeting customers with high churn propensity scores.
Activate the high-risk audience to your preferred channel to deliver a personalized win-back offer.
Configure a Customer AI model to predict upsell likelihood and run it against your ingested customer profiles.
Build an audience in Segment Builder using the propensity scores generated by Customer AI to target high-likelihood upsell candidates.
Activate that audience to your email or advertising destination to deliver a personalized upsell campaign.
Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate churn propensity scores for each customer profile.
Build an audience of high-churn-risk customers by filtering profiles where the propensity score exceeds your defined threshold.
Activate that audience in a Journey Optimizer campaign to deliver personalized retention offers before those customers churn.
Define conversion events in Attribution AI by specifying the goal actions such as purchases or sign-ups you want to measure.
Map your marketing touchpoints to the conversion events to identify which channels influenced each conversion.
Configure and run the Attribution AI model to generate attribution scores across all mapped touchpoints and channels.
Analyze the attribution scores and channel ROI insights in the dashboard to optimize your marketing spend allocation.
Configure an Attribution AI model instance by selecting your conversion events and mapping your marketing touchpoint datasets.
Run the Attribution AI model to generate algorithmic credit scores across all marketing channels and touchpoints.
Analyze the channel performance insights dashboard to identify which channels drive the most conversion credit.
Reallocate your marketing budget toward the highest-performing channels based on the Attribution AI scores.
Configure an Attribution AI model instance by selecting your conversion events and specifying the lookback window and attribution model type.
Run the Attribution AI model to generate channel and touchpoint influence scores across your customer journeys.
Export the Attribution AI scores dataset to Customer Journey Analytics by connecting it as a CJA data source.
Build an executive dashboard in CJA using the attribution scores to visualize channel performance and marketing ROI.
Navigate to Query Service in Experience Platform and open the Query Editor to begin writing SQL.
Write a SQL query that selects the marketing channel field and counts distinct visitor IDs from your experience event dataset.
Run the query to execute it against the Platform dataset and retrieve the unique visitor counts grouped by marketing channel.
Review the results table in the Query Editor and export or save the query for scheduled recurring analysis.
Ingest a batch of customer records into an Experience Platform dataset via batch ingestion.
Open Query Service and write a SQL query targeting the ingested dataset to check field values and row counts.
Run the query and review the results to identify null values, duplicates, or unexpected field distributions.
Use the query findings to confirm data quality or flag issues before enabling the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile.
Ingest raw behavioral event data into Experience Platform and confirm it lands in a queryable dataset.
Write a SQL query in Query Service that aggregates event data to identify high-value customers by spend or engagement metrics.
Execute the query as a CTAS statement to materialize the results into a new derived dataset in Platform.
Enable the derived dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so high-value customer attributes are available for segmentation and activation.
Retrieve your Query Service credentials from the Experience Platform UI to enable external client connections.
Connect Tableau Desktop to Query Service using the retrieved credentials and PostgreSQL connector.
Write and run SQL queries in Tableau to pull audience membership and engagement data from Platform datasets.
Build an interactive audience performance visualization in Tableau using the queried data.
Open Query Service and write a SQL query that joins purchase event data with customer profiles to find all customers.
Filter the query results to return only customers whose last purchase date is more than 30 days ago.
Save the query results as a new derived dataset containing the lapsed customer IDs.
Use that derived dataset to build an audience in Segment Builder and activate it to a re-engagement destination.
Connect to Query Service and explore the raw event history dataset to understand the available behavioral signals.
Write and run SQL queries in Query Service to compute churn-indicator features such as days since last activity and session frequency.
Save the query output as a new derived dataset in Experience Platform by using the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement.
Enable the derived churn-indicator dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so the features are available for segmentation and AI models.
Configure a streaming source connector to ingest real-time events into an Experience Platform dataset mapped to your XDM schema.
Allow the streaming ingestion to run until a representative set of events has landed in the dataset.
Open Query Service and write a SQL query against the dataset to inspect field names, data types, and null counts across the ingested events.
Compare the query results against the expected XDM schema definition to confirm all fields are correctly mapped and no schema violations exist.
Identify the contractually restricted third-party data fields in your existing XDM schema.
Apply the appropriate DULE data usage labels to those schema fields to mark them as restricted.
Create a data usage policy that references those labels to enforce contractual restrictions on downstream use.
Verify that the policy triggers a violation warning when restricted fields are activated to a disallowed destination.
Open an existing profile schema in the Schema Editor and identify fields that contain personally identifiable information such as name, email, and phone number.
Apply the appropriate data usage labels, such as I1 or I2, to each identified PII field to mark them as sensitive personal data.
Save the labeled schema so that the applied labels are propagated to any datasets created from that schema.
Create a data usage policy that references those sensitivity labels to enforce restrictions on how those PII fields can be used or activated.
Open an existing XDM event schema in the Schema Editor and locate the device ID fields used for identity stitching.
Apply appropriate data usage labels, such as I1 or I2, to those device ID fields to mark them as identity-linked and restricted.
Create a data usage policy that references those labels and prohibits their use in identity-stitching operations across datasets.
Enforce the policy so that any attempt to stitch profiles using the labeled device ID fields is blocked and flagged for review.
Identify sensitive schema fields in your dataset that must not be shared with advertising platforms.
Apply restrictive data usage labels to those schema fields to mark them as restricted for advertising.
Create a data usage policy that references those labels and defines the prohibited marketing action of exporting to ad networks.
Enable the policy so that Platform enforces it and blocks any activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
Apply restrictive data usage labels to schema fields containing sensitive personal data.
Create a data usage policy that prohibits activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
Build an audience segment that incorporates the restricted labeled fields from the schema.
Attempt to activate the audience to an advertising destination and confirm the governance policy automatically blocks it.
Apply data usage labels to sensitive schema fields to classify them as restricted for advertising use.
Create a data usage policy that blocks activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
Attempt to activate an audience containing the labeled fields to an ad destination to trigger policy evaluation.
Review the policy violation alert that blocks the activation, confirming governance enforcement is working correctly.
Apply HIPAA-aligned data usage labels to sensitive health-related schema fields to mark them as restricted for marketing use.
Create data usage policies that block those labeled fields from being activated to advertising or third-party marketing destinations.
Build a compliant audience using only unlabeled or permitted fields in Segment Builder, respecting all governance constraints.
Activate the audience to an approved healthcare marketing destination, allowing Platform to enforce policies and block any violations.
Submit a GDPR data access request through the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity.
Privacy Service fans out the request to all configured Experience Platform products and data stores holding that customer's data.
Each product retrieves the matching records and packages them into a downloadable data file.
Download and deliver the compiled data export to the customer to fulfill the GDPR access request.
Submit a CCPA deletion job through Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity values to target their data.
Privacy Service validates the request and fans it out to all connected Platform services that hold the customer's data.
Each Platform service locates and deletes the customer's data records tied to the submitted identities.
Privacy Service marks the job as complete and returns a confirmation so you can document compliance with the deletion request.
Install the AEP Privacy JavaScript library on your website by adding the script tag to your page.
Configure the library with your organization ID so it can route consent signals to the correct Experience Cloud solutions.
Capture visitor opt-out interactions on your website and pass them to the library's opt-out API.
The library forwards the opt-out signals to Privacy Service, which propagates the consent preferences across all connected AEP solutions.
Authenticate with the Privacy Service API by obtaining an access token using your IMS organization credentials.
Submit bulk privacy job requests by sending POST calls to the API with customer identity details and regulation type.
Poll the API with the returned job IDs to monitor processing status until all privacy jobs reach completion.
Retrieve the completed job results from the API and confirm that the requested data access or deletion has been fulfilled.
Register an Adobe I/O integration and configure a webhook endpoint to receive Privacy Service event notifications.
Subscribe the integration to Privacy Service events so job completion notifications are routed to your webhook.
Submit a GDPR or CCPA deletion request through the Privacy Service API to initiate the deletion job.
Receive the real-time job completion event at your webhook and confirm the deletion request was fulfilled.
Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert types.
Select the segment job failure alert type to monitor audience evaluation errors.
Subscribe to the alert by entering your notification preferences, such as email or in-platform notifications.
Receive an immediate notification when an audience evaluation job fails so you can investigate and resolve the issue.
Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert rules.
Select the ingestion delay metric alert rule that matches your critical daily data pipeline.
Configure the alert threshold and notification channel, then enable the alert rule.
Receive a notification when ingestion delay exceeds the threshold, confirming the pipeline is actively monitored.
Connect your high-priority campaign destination in Experience Platform to ensure it is ready to receive audience activations.
Activate your high-priority campaign audience to that connected destination to initiate the data flow.
Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and subscribe to the destination activation failure alert type.
Receive an immediate notification if the activation fails so your team can investigate and resolve the issue quickly.
Ingest a batch of customer data into an Experience Platform dataset using batch ingestion.
Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard in the Platform UI to locate the ingestion job.
Open the batch run details to review the number of records ingested and any failed records.
Confirm the batch status shows as Success before proceeding with downstream processing.
Build a new audience in Segment Builder and publish it to make it available for activation.
Connect an advertising destination and activate the published audience to that destination.
Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard and open the Segment Activation view to find the active dataflow.
Review the dataflow run details, checking ingested identity counts and any errors to confirm successful delivery.
Navigate to the Sources catalog in Experience Platform and open the active source connection you want to investigate.
Open the Dataflows tab for that source connection to view the list of recent dataflow runs and their statuses.
Select a failed or partial dataflow run to inspect its detailed run history, including ingested record counts and error messages.
Use the error codes and failed-record details surfaced in the run report to identify and resolve the root cause of the missing records.
Open the Admin Console and confirm the team member has been added as a user in the organization.
Navigate to the Permissions UI and open the role assigned to that team member.
Add the AI Assistant access and AI Assistant Operational Insights permissions to that role.
Save the updated role so the team member can now access AI Assistant in Experience Platform.
Ask AI Assistant to explain what merge policies are and how they control which data fragments are prioritized in a unified profile.
Ask AI Assistant to describe the difference between timestamp-ordered and custom attribute precedence merge strategies.
Ask AI Assistant how selecting a specific merge policy affects the attributes and identities returned during a Real-Time Customer Profile lookup.
Use the AI Assistant's explanations to configure the appropriate merge policy for your dataset and validate profile lookups return the expected data.
Open AI Assistant and ask it for a step-by-step guide on activating an audience to a new destination.
Follow the AI Assistant's instructions to navigate to Destinations and configure a new destination connection.
Use the guidance provided to select your target audience and map the required identity and attribute fields.
Complete the activation flow as directed by AI Assistant to start delivering your audience to the new destination.
Ask AI Assistant why your streaming segment is not evaluating in real time and describe the observed behavior.
Review AI Assistant's explanation of common causes such as missing streaming ingestion setup or unsupported segment operators.
Follow AI Assistant's guided steps to verify that the source dataset is streaming-enabled and the segment criteria support streaming evaluation.
Confirm the fix by monitoring the segment evaluation logs and asking AI Assistant to validate the updated configuration.
Open AI Assistant in the Experience Platform UI within your sandbox environment.
Ask AI Assistant how many audiences currently have zero profiles in this sandbox.
AI Assistant queries operational metadata and returns the count of empty audiences with their names.
Review the list of zero-profile audiences and take corrective action such as deleting or rebuilding them.
Open AI Assistant in Journey Optimizer and confirm it is connected to your production sandbox.
Ask AI Assistant which journeys are currently live and actively using your target audience by name.
Review the list of journeys returned by AI Assistant, including their statuses and entry conditions referencing that audience.
Use the journey names provided to navigate directly to each journey and take any necessary action.
Open AI Assistant in Experience Platform and ask it to list all audiences that have never been activated to any destination.
Review the AI Assistant's response to confirm the full list of inactive audiences returned.
Select each unused audience from the list in the Audiences UI to verify it is safe to remove.
Delete the confirmed unused audiences to clean up the audience inventory and reduce clutter.
Ask AI Assistant to list all audiences with zero profile counts in your sandbox.
Review the returned list of empty audiences and confirm they are safe to delete before migration.
Delete the identified zero-profile audiences to clean up the sandbox environment.
Verify with AI Assistant that no unused audiences remain before proceeding with the sandbox migration.
Identify the schema attribute you are considering deleting from your data model.
Ask AI Assistant which datasets, segments, and journeys depend on that schema attribute.
Review the full list of dependent objects returned by AI Assistant to assess the impact of deletion.
Remove or update all dependent objects confirmed by AI Assistant before safely deleting the schema attribute.
Identify the schema field you plan to modify or remove in Experience Platform.
Ask AI Assistant to trace the lineage of that field across datasets, segments, and journeys.
Review the downstream assets AI Assistant surfaces that depend on the field, such as audiences and activated destinations.
Use the impact report to safely update or deprecate the field without breaking dependent workflows.
Ingest partner-provided financial segment data into Experience Platform using a partner data source connector.
Map the partner attributes to your existing XDM schema fields to align them with known customer profiles.
Use identity matching to merge the partner financial attributes into unified real-time customer profiles.
Build audiences segmented by the enriched financial attributes and activate them to your marketing destinations.

workflows.source: Partner Data / Personalize for unknown visitors
steps: Integrate a partner data provider to supply identity signals for anonymous website visitors with no known profile.
Map partner-supplied attributes and identifiers to your XDM schema to build temporary profiles for those unknown visitors.
Build an audience segment using the partner-resolved attributes to classify anonymous visitors by interest or intent.
Activate the anonymous visitor audience to your web personalization destination to deliver tailored content in real time.
Ingest partner-provided enrichment data into Experience Platform by onboarding partner attributes to your existing customer profiles.
Build a seed audience of your highest-value existing customers using those enriched profile attributes in Segment Builder.
Use partner lookalike modeling to expand the seed audience into a net-new prospecting audience of unknown users who resemble your best customers.
Activate the lookalike prospecting audience to offsite advertising destinations to drive new customer acquisition.

workflows.source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
steps: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select the abandoned cart re-engagement playbook that matches your goal.
Create an instance of the playbook to generate its supporting technical assets including schemas and datasets.
Review the auto-generated journey, audiences, and offer configurations produced by the playbook instance.
Publish the playbook assets to your sandbox so the journey and audiences are ready for activation.

workflows.source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
steps: Browse the Use Case Playbooks gallery and select a churn prevention playbook that matches your business goal.
Create an instance of the churn prevention playbook inside the inspiration sandbox.
Review the generated assets, including journeys, segments, and schemas, produced by the playbook instance.
Publish the playbook assets to your sandbox so they are ready to configure and activate.

workflows.source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
steps: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select a B2B account nurture playbook as your starting point.
Create an instance of the playbook to generate its pre-built assets, including schemas, segments, and journeys.
Customize the generated assets to align with your specific ABM campaign targets and messaging strategy.
Publish the finalized playbook assets to your sandbox and activate the account audience to your ABM destination.
Browse the playbook gallery and create an instance of a playbook to generate its artifacts.
Review the generated artifacts, such as schemas, datasets, and journeys, inside the playbook instance.
Publish the playbook package from the source sandbox to make the artifacts available for export.
Import the published package into your development sandbox to begin building with those assets.
Create a dedicated sandbox in Experience Platform to serve as the playbook inspiration environment.
Add the sandbox to the required product profile in Admin Console so that users can access it.
Assign the necessary playbook permissions to the product profile in the Permissions UI.
Navigate to Use Case Playbooks within the configured sandbox to browse and instantiate playbooks.
Create a custom dashboard in Experience Platform and give it a name and description to identify its purpose.
Add widgets to the dashboard that pull real-time data for profile counts and audience sizes from the profile store.
Add additional widgets displaying activation metrics such as audiences activated per destination and segment membership trends.
Save and publish the dashboard so stakeholders can monitor KPI trends across profiles, audiences, and activations.
Create a custom dashboard in the Dashboards UI and give it a name that reflects its executive audience.
Add widgets that display segment health metrics such as audience size, growth trends, and profile coverage.
Add destination delivery widgets showing activation success rates, dataflow run statuses, and records delivered per destination.
Save and share the completed dashboard so executives can monitor segment health and delivery performance in one view.
Create a custom dashboard in Experience Platform and give it a meaningful name for tracking ingestion health.
Add widgets that query batch ingestion metrics, such as records ingested, failed batches, and job status counts.
Configure each widget to filter data by day so that success and failure rates reflect the correct daily time window.
Save and publish the dashboard so stakeholders can monitor daily batch job success rates in real time.
Review the test dataset in the Data Lake to confirm it is expired and no longer referenced by any active schemas or segments.
Check that no active destinations or journeys depend on the dataset before proceeding with deletion.
Submit a dataset expiration request in the Data Hygiene workspace, specifying the target dataset and deletion date.
Verify the dataset has been fully removed from the Data Lake by confirming it no longer appears in the dataset inventory.
Monitor batch ingestion status in the platform to identify a failed or incorrect batch containing bad records.
Note the batch ID of the failed ingestion so you can target it precisely for deletion.
Submit a batch delete request using that batch ID to remove the incorrect records from the dataset.
Verify the deletion is complete by confirming the records no longer appear in the dataset or unified profiles.
Navigate to the Data Lifecycle workspace and select the temporary campaign dataset you want to expire.
Create a dataset expiration request by specifying the exact date on which the dataset should be deleted.
Submit the expiration request so that Platform schedules the automatic deletion of the dataset on that date.
Verify the scheduled expiration appears on the dataset record, confirming it will be automatically removed on the configured date.
Review your dataset and confirm which profiles lack authenticated identities and qualify as pseudonymous.
Navigate to Data Hygiene settings and configure a pseudonymous profile expiration policy set to 30 days of inactivity.
Platform evaluates all pseudonymous profiles against the 30-day inactivity threshold and flags expired records for deletion.
Expired pseudonymous profiles are automatically removed from the profile store, freeing storage and keeping data clean.
Connect to Query Service and run SQL queries against your datasets to surface records that have not been updated beyond your staleness threshold.
Review the query results to confirm the identified records are genuinely stale and eligible for deletion, noting their primary identities.
Submit a record delete hygiene job in Experience Platform using the confirmed identities of those stale records.
Monitor the hygiene job status until completion and re-run validation queries to confirm the stale records have been removed from the dataset.

workflows.source: Marketing Workflows / Plan and size campaign
steps: Build a candidate audience in Segment Builder and review the estimated profile count to confirm the campaign is sized correctly.
Inspect each profile's active journey memberships to identify any customers already enrolled in a conflicting journey.
Exclude or suppress the conflicting profiles from the campaign audience to prevent overlapping communications.
Finalize the cleaned audience and launch the campaign journey, confident there are no messaging conflicts.
Build an audience of lapsed customers who have not engaged within a defined time window.
Design the re-engagement journey in Journey Optimizer, adding the audience as the entry trigger.
Configure the journey steps with personalized messages, wait nodes, and channel actions such as email or push.
Review and publish the journey so that qualifying customers begin receiving re-engagement communications.
Capture real-time cart abandonment events from your website or app using the Web SDK or Mobile SDK.
Define a segment of customers who added items to their cart but did not complete a purchase within a set time window.
Build a Journey Optimizer journey triggered by the cart abandonment event for that audience.
Send a personalized push notification reminding each customer of their abandoned cart items to drive conversion.
Create an audience of customers who have newly qualified for a higher loyalty tier based on their recent purchase activity.
Build a journey in Journey Optimizer triggered by entry into that loyalty tier upgrade audience.
Author the tier upgrade notification message with personalized content reflecting the customer's new tier benefits.
Publish the journey so newly qualified customers automatically receive the tier upgrade notification across their preferred channel.
Open Customer Journey Analytics and select the product launch date range to scope the analysis.
Load the cross-channel attribution panel to see how each channel contributed to conversions during the launch.
Compare attribution models to identify which channels drove the most assisted and last-touch conversions.
Export the KPI summary and share the report with stakeholders to inform future campaign investment decisions.
Open Adobe Marketing Agent and ask it to retrieve the current size of your target audience segment.
Review the returned audience size data to confirm the audience meets the minimum threshold for your campaign.
Ask Adobe Marketing Agent to scan all live journeys for any that are already targeting the same audience segment.
Review the identified conflicts and adjust journey entry conditions or audience assignments to eliminate overlap before launch.
Navigate to Segment Match in Experience Platform and initiate a new connection request to your media partner organization.
Provide the partner organization's IMS Org ID so the platform can route the connection request to the correct recipient.
Wait for the media partner organization to review and accept the incoming connection request on their end.
Once the connection is confirmed, select and send the target audience segments to the media partner through the established Segment Match connection.
Apply data usage labels to the schema fields that make up the audience to mark them as restricted for sharing.
Create a data usage policy that governs how those labeled fields may be exported to partners.
Configure a Segment Match connection by sending a partner invite and agreeing on shared overlap conditions.
Activate the labeled audience through Segment Match, allowing platform governance to enforce the export policy before data leaves.
Build a high-intent retail buyer audience in Segment Builder using purchase behavior and browsing signals.
Set up a Segment Match connection by sending a partnership invitation to your co-marketing partner's AEP sandbox.
Select the high-intent retail buyer audience and configure the match keys for secure overlap estimation with the partner.
Approve and activate the share so the partner receives the matched audience in their sandbox for co-marketing campaigns.
Review and accept the incoming segment share request from your data partner in Segment Match.
Verify the received audience data is mapped correctly to your own identity namespace and schema fields.
Enrich the accepted partner audience by merging it with your first-party profile attributes in the Segment Builder.
Activate the combined prospecting audience to your advertising destination to launch the prospecting campaign.
Build an audience segment of the customers you want to evaluate for potential partner sharing.
Send overlap estimation request to your partner's sandbox using Segment Match pre-share insights.
Review the estimated overlap count and percentage to assess mutual value before committing to the share.
Decide whether to proceed with the full audience share to your partner based on the overlap insights.
Ingest customer data from all your online and offline sources into Experience Platform.
Stitch the ingested data into unified real-time customer profiles using the identity graph.
Build targeted segments from those unified profiles using the Segment Builder.
Activate the resulting audiences to your advertising and marketing destinations.
Detect customers who entered but did not complete the checkout flow using real-time streaming event data.
Use Customer AI to score those customers by their likelihood to convert if re-engaged.
Build a high-priority audience from customers with strong conversion propensity scores.
Launch a personalized re-engagement journey across email, push, and paid channels to bring them back.
Ingest customer behavioral and transactional data into Experience Platform to build unified real-time profiles.
Configure and run a Customer AI propensity model to score each customer's likelihood to churn.
Build a high-risk churn audience by segmenting profiles that exceed the defined churn propensity score threshold.
Activate the churn-risk audience to email and advertising destinations to deliver targeted retention offers in real time.
Collect real-time behavioral events from your web and mobile apps by routing them through the Edge Network using the Web or Mobile SDK.
Edge Network forwards the streaming event data into Experience Platform, where it is merged into a unified real-time customer profile via the identity graph.
Build an audience in Segment Builder that evaluates those streaming profile attributes and events in real time.
Activate the audience to your chosen destination so personalized experiences are delivered immediately as customers qualify.
Ingest customer data from all channels and sources into Real-Time CDP using batch and streaming connectors.
Stitch the ingested data fragments into unified real-time customer profiles using the identity graph.
Build target audiences from those unified profiles using Real-Time CDP's segment builder.
Activate the audiences to advertising, email, and other destinations to deliver consistent cross-channel experiences.
Define business goals, data sources, and success metrics during the planning phase with stakeholders.
Implement schemas, datasets, and data ingestion pipelines to bring customer data into Experience Platform.
Launch the project by activating audiences and journeys to deliver experiences across channels.
Monitor performance, refine segments, and iterate on the solution during the ongoing operations phase.
Ingest customer behavioral and transactional data into Experience Platform to build a rich real-time customer profile.
Read the known customer's live profile attributes, including purchase history, preferences, and recent interactions.
Use offer decisioning to select the most contextually relevant offer based on those real-time profile attributes.
Deliver the personalized offer to the customer at the moment of engagement across their active channel.
Batch-ingest CRM customer records into Experience Platform using a CRM source connector.
The identity graph stitches ingested records into unified real-time customer profiles across devices and channels.
Build a target segment from those unified profiles using Segment Builder based on CRM attributes.
Activate the resulting audience to your email destination to deliver a personalized campaign.
Connect omnichannel data sources such as web, mobile, and in-store to Experience Platform and ingest the data into datasets.
Create a Customer Journey Analytics connection linking those Platform datasets to make them available for analysis.
Build a Data View in Customer Journey Analytics to define the metrics and dimensions needed for funnel analysis.
Create a Fallout or Flow visualization in Analysis Workspace to analyze conversion steps and identify drop-off points across channels.
Identify the schema fields that capture customer consent and opt-out preferences in your dataset.
Apply consent-related data usage labels to those sensitive schema fields to mark them as restricted.
Create a data usage policy that enforces opt-out restrictions and blocks activation for labeled fields.
Activate the audience to a destination, triggering policy enforcement that honors customer opt-out preferences before delivery.
Apply data usage labels to behavioral data schema fields to mark them as restricted for third-party sharing.
Connect a third-party partner destination in the Destinations catalog to make it available for policy enforcement.
Create a data usage policy that references those labels and prohibits export to third-party partner destinations.
Enable the policy so that any attempt to activate labeled behavioral data to that destination is automatically blocked.
Apply sensitive financial data usage labels to the relevant schema fields to mark them as restricted.
Create a data usage policy that references those labels and blocks activation to advertising destinations.
Enable the policy so it is enforced across all downstream activation workflows.
Attempt to activate a dataset containing those labeled fields to a destination and confirm the policy blocks the action.
Identify the schema fields that contain device IDs used in identity stitching across your customer profiles.
Apply identity-stitching restriction data usage labels to those device ID fields in the schema editor.
Create a data usage policy that blocks fields carrying those labels from being exported to partner destinations.
Activate an audience to a partner destination and confirm the policy enforcement prevents the labeled device ID fields from being shared.
Create custom identity namespaces for each brand's loyalty program identifier in the Identity Service namespace registry.
Define an XDM schema for the multi-brand loyalty program and add the loyalty ID fields mapped to their respective custom namespaces.
Label each loyalty ID schema field with its corresponding identity namespace to mark primary and secondary identities.
Ingest loyalty member records so the identity graph stitches cross-brand profiles into unified customer identities.
Collect anonymous browsing events from an unidentified visitor using the Web SDK, assigning them a temporary ECID.
Store those anonymous behavioral events in a dataset linked to the ECID in the identity graph.
When the visitor authenticates, capture their known identifier such as email and link it to the existing ECID.
Identity Service merges the anonymous and authenticated identities into a single unified real-time customer profile.

workflows.source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
steps: Create an XDM Experience Event schema and enable it for Real-Time Customer Profile.
Create a streaming dataset using that schema to receive continuous event data.
Connect a streaming source or Web SDK to ingest live events into the dataset.
Experience Platform merges each incoming event into unified real-time customer profiles via the identity graph.
Create a schema field to store the computed average order value on the profile.
Define a computed attribute rule that calculates the average order value across all purchase events in the last 90 days.
Enable and publish the computed attribute so the platform begins processing historical and streaming event data.
Use the computed average order value attribute to build audience segments and personalize customer experiences.
Build a segment identifying all test accounts by filtering profiles on a known test attribute or identity namespace.
Confirm the segment population is accurate by previewing the estimated profile count before proceeding.
Submit a bulk profile delete job targeting that segment to remove all matched test account profiles from the store.
Verify the deletion job completes successfully and confirm no test profiles remain before promoting the sandbox to production.
Enable multiple datasets for Real-Time Customer Profile so their schemas contribute to the union schema.
Open the union schema view in the Platform UI to see all merged fields from contributing datasets.
Inspect the identity field section of the union schema to confirm each contributing dataset includes the required identity descriptors.
Resolve any datasets missing required identity fields by updating their schemas and re-enabling them for Profile.
Connect to Query Service and identify the Platform datasets containing customer purchase event data.
Write and run a SQL query that aggregates total spend, order counts, and average order value per customer ID.
Save the query results as a derived dataset in Platform to persist the computed lifetime value scores.
Build an audience in Segment Builder using the lifetime value scores from the derived dataset and activate it to a destination.
Ingest raw customer event history, including browsing and purchase interactions, into an Experience Platform dataset.
Write a SQL query in Query Service that aggregates event data to compute product affinity scores per customer.
Run the query as a Create Table As Select statement to materialize the affinity scores into a new derived dataset.
Use the derived product affinity dataset as a feature input for segmentation or AI model training workflows.
Ingest migrated data into the new schema dataset so records are available for querying in Experience Platform.
Write a SQL query in Query Service that joins the old and new schema datasets on a shared identity key.
Execute the query to compare field values across both schemas and surface any mapping discrepancies in the results.
Review the query output to confirm all fields are correctly mapped and the migrated data matches the expected schema structure.
Navigate to Query Service in Experience Platform and export your PostgreSQL credentials including host, port, and authentication details.
Open Tableau Desktop and create a new connection using the exported Query Service credentials to establish a live connection to the platform.
Write and run a SQL query in Tableau to pull attribution and campaign performance data from Experience Platform datasets.
Build an attribution performance report in Tableau by visualizing the queried data with charts, filters, and calculated metrics.
Open the Monitoring dashboard in Experience Platform and navigate to the Data Ingestion section.
Select the failed batch from the list of recent ingestion runs to open its detail view.
Review the batch status and identify which records failed during ingestion.
Expand the failed record entries to read the specific error messages explaining why ingestion failed.
Navigate to a destination dataflow in the Platform UI and open the alerts subscription panel.
Subscribe to the destination dataflow failure alert to enable notifications for that dataflow.
Wait for the dataflow to fail, triggering the alert notification in the Platform alerts inbox.
Open the triggered alert notification and acknowledge it to mark the incident as reviewed.
Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard and open the dataflow run history for the relevant source connector.
Identify the recurring failed runs and inspect the error details to confirm a schema mismatch is causing ingestion failures.
Update the source schema or field mappings in the dataflow configuration to resolve the mismatch.
Trigger a new dataflow run and confirm in the monitoring dashboard that data ingests successfully without schema errors.
Export the list of customers requiring erasure from your CRM, collecting their identity values such as email and customer ID.
Submit a bulk privacy delete job to Privacy Service via API, providing each customer's identity namespace and value pairs.
Privacy Service fans out the delete request to all configured Experience Platform services, including Profile, Identity, and data lake.
Monitor the job status in Privacy Service until all delete requests complete, confirming the customers' data has been fully erased.
Submit a DSAR access request via the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity details and the datasets to search.
Privacy Service fans out the request to all configured Experience Cloud products and retrieves the customer's matching data records.
Privacy Service compiles the retrieved records into a complete data export package once all products have responded.
Download the finished export package from Privacy Service and deliver it to the customer to fulfill the DSAR.
Register a webhook endpoint in your system to receive incoming HTTP event notifications from Adobe Privacy Service.
Subscribe the webhook to Privacy Service job status events using the Event Notifications configuration in Experience Platform.
Submit a privacy job request through Privacy Service to generate a real status event payload.
Receive the event notification at your webhook endpoint and trigger your automated downstream workflow based on the job status.

workflows.source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
steps: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select a loyalty re-engagement playbook that matches your campaign goal.
Create an instance of the playbook to generate its supporting assets, including schemas, datasets, and segments.
Review and publish the generated templates and audience assets to your development sandbox.
Use the generated journey template to launch a personalized loyalty re-engagement journey for at-risk customers.
Browse the use case playbook gallery and create an instance of a playbook that matches your campaign scenario.
Review the playbook-generated assets, including schemas, datasets, and audiences, in the inspirational sandbox.
Publish the playbook package so its assets become available for import into another sandbox.
Import the published package into your development sandbox to begin customizing schemas and audiences for your use case.
Create a new sandbox in Experience Platform to serve as the dedicated environment for Use Case Playbooks.
Add the sandbox to the appropriate product profile in Admin Console so users can access it.
Assign the required Use Case Playbooks permissions to the role in the Permissions UI for that sandbox.
Open the Use Case Playbooks catalog in the configured sandbox to browse and launch available playbooks.

workflows.source: Partner Data / Personalize for unknown visitors
steps: Integrate a partner data provider to resolve anonymous visitor identifiers and attach partner-supplied attributes to the unknown visitor's profile.
Use the partner-resolved attributes to build an audience segment representing anonymous visitors with specific interests or intent signals.
Configure a personalization destination to deliver tailored landing page content based on the anonymous visitor's segment membership.
Serve the personalized landing page experience to the anonymous visitor in real time using the activated partner-enriched audience.
Ingest partner-provided prospect data into Experience Platform using partner data connectors to access new potential customers.
Enrich your existing high-value customer profiles with partner attributes to build a lookalike seed audience in Segment Builder.
Expand the seed audience into a partner-enriched lookalike audience targeting net-new customers who resemble your best customers.
Activate the lookalike audience to your DSP destination to run offsite prospecting campaigns and acquire new customers.
Query the profile dataset using Query Service to calculate the percentage of profiles that contain a valid email address.
Save the query results as a derived dataset that exposes the email completeness metric for visualization.
Create a custom dashboard in the Dashboards UI and add a new widget pointed at the derived dataset.
Configure the widget to display the email completeness percentage so stakeholders can monitor profile quality over time.
Create a custom dashboard in Experience Platform and add widgets tracking activation job statuses across all configured destinations.
Configure each widget to query activation metrics such as records sent, failed, and skipped per destination channel.
Arrange and save the dashboard layout to display success rates side by side for each channel.
Share the published dashboard with stakeholders to monitor destination health and activation success rates in real time.
Navigate to the License Usage dashboard in Experience Platform to view your current entitlement limits and consumption metrics.
Identify the relevant profile volume widgets and configure them to display the metrics most critical to your entitlement thresholds.
Create a custom dashboard and add widgets that track profile count, addressable audiences, and richness against licensed limits.
Set alert thresholds on the dashboard so your team is notified when profile volume approaches or exceeds entitlement limits.
Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for your customer profiles.
Verify that the propensity score attributes have been written to the unified Real-Time Customer Profile dataset.
Create a custom dashboard in Platform and add widgets that query the propensity score dataset.
Visualise the propensity score distributions across your customer base directly within the custom Platform dashboard.
Identify the mis-mapped ingestion batch in the dataset activity view and note its batch ID.
Submit a batch delete request using that batch ID to remove the incorrect records from the dataset and profile store.
Confirm the batch deletion is complete and verify the mis-mapped records no longer appear in the dataset.
Re-ingest the corrected source file into the same dataset so accurate records populate the customer profiles.
Identify the time-boxed campaign event datasets whose data should be automatically removed after a defined retention period.
Navigate to Data Hygiene in the Platform UI and create a dataset expiration request for the first campaign dataset, setting the expiry date.
Repeat the dataset expiration configuration for each remaining campaign event dataset, assigning the appropriate expiry date to each.
Review and confirm all scheduled dataset expirations so Platform automatically deletes each campaign dataset on its designated expiry date.
Navigate to the Datasets inventory in Experience Platform and review each dataset's storage size and last ingestion date.
Flag datasets that are large, inactive, or no longer needed by comparing them against current business use cases and data retention requirements.
Set a dataset expiration date on each identified obsolete dataset to schedule it for automatic deletion.
Confirm the expiration schedule and monitor the Data Hygiene dashboard to verify that targeted datasets are removed and storage is reclaimed.
Build an audience of your key customer segment in Experience Platform using Segment Builder.
Send a connection request to your data partner through Segment Match to initiate the overlap estimation process.
Review the pre-share overlap estimates to see how many identities your audience shares with the partner's audience.
Use the overlap insights to decide whether the partner audience share is worth pursuing before activating any data.

Receive and accept the incoming connection request from the CPG brand in the Segment Match UI to establish the partnership.

Share the agreed audience segments with the CPG brand partner to activate joint campaign targeting across both organizations.
